newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says guerrillas responsible for Lima storming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says guerrillas responsible for Lima storming.

text.p: The United States said Marxist guerrillas who were holding hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima bore full responsibility for the storming of the building by Peruvian troops on Tuesday.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns stopped short of directly applauding the decision to send in the troops, but said Washington would not "second-guess" the Peruvian government on the issue.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas had been holding 72 hostages for four months. Local radio in Lima said all the guerrillas and one hostage were killed in the rescue operation.

"One thing is clear: the MRTA bears the full and complete responsibility for this outcome," Burns said in a statement. Asked if Peruvian authorities had made the right decision, he said: "We are not going to second-guess the Peruvian government."
Burns said Secretary of State Madeleine Albright planned to write on Tuesday evening to Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, one of the hostages, "congratulating him on his rescue".

Burns said the United States, which throughout the crisis had urged that no concessions should be made to "terrorists", had not known in advance about the storming and had played no role in it or given any advice.
